value.falsifier_check: DONE when (1) the tester's raise and clear of a seal trouble share ONE identity derived by one function at one address that both cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py and cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.py call; (2) a proof under a temp log root asserts that a seal turned red by the ladder and green by a HAND seal (TesterDevice.run_proof) leaves nothing outstanding for cc, and that a green reseal with nothing raised emits no clear; (3) the raise/clear census over ~/.cairn/logs/tester/0 restricted to emissions after the build commit shows every raised identity cleared under the same key once its seal is green and no clear without a prior raise. RED if any clear is emitted for a key nothing raised, or if the two files still spell the identity separately. WRONG INTENT if the two keys were meant as two troubles (component-level roll-up vs per-proof) — then the fix is a recorded pairing between them, not a merge; the open question decides which.
value.missing_check: One point is deliberately NOT wrapped and is the open question: whether the one identity is per PROOF (the store's grain; finer; what a hand seal knows) or per COMPONENT (the ladder's grain; what ticket 4d9115eb04cd's rung-3 language names). value.better_approach: Looked: dropping one emitter outright (the ladder raises, the store never announces) is smaller, but the store's announce is the only emitter a HAND seal ever reaches, and hand seals are how every voyage seals. Keeping both emitters and unifying the KEY is the smallest change that makes the fold correct.
value.hidden_assumption: That the trouble fold matches clears to raises by identity string alone. If the drain host (absent — trouble-drain-has-no-host-the-beat-backstop-is-prose) ever folds by proof path instead, the mismatch is invisible; measured today it is not folding at all, so the log tree IS the record.
value.prior_art: In-house: reseal.py's CLEARS_FOR comment (2026-09-13) fixed the RECIPIENT of the clear after 11 of 12 seal-red troubles stayed open — same fold, a neighbouring axis; ticket 9579a6f9cec6 (2026-09-08) moved the store's clear from a bus request to an emission. Neither touched the identity. Ticket a48f95c51a41 (a validation is one current record) is the store side. No ticket in the corpus names the raise/clear identity mismatch (grep seal-red + validation-verdict-changed over tickets/: four hits, none about identity).
value.real_collision: None exclusive-and-terminal. Component-level identity (the ladder's) and proof-level identity (the store's) are both defensible; the ruling on rung-3 reds (4d9115eb04cd) speaks of a component's seal-red — so the per-proof key must still let a component-level reader roll up. A distinction to record, not a collision.
